question.text: Which of the following best describes the actions taken by the exchange/clearing corporation for margin violations in the equity derivatives segment?

answer.text: The exchange/clearing corporation can levy penalties, withdraw trading or clearing facilities, close out open positions, and invoke deposits and collateral of the defaulting member
Only advisory notices are sent and no monetary or operational action is taken
No action is taken because margin compliance is voluntary in the F&O segment
Only the client is penalised and the broker has no exposure to disciplinary action

explanation.text: The Logic: The Series VIII workbook (pages 170-171 and 179-180) supports exchange/clearing-corporation level action for margin violations, including penalties and disciplinary measures, withdrawal of trading or clearing facilities, close-out of open positions, and invocation of deposits and collateral of the defaulting member. The Trap: The workbook pages checked do not attribute these specific margin-violation actions to SEBI or to broker licence suspension; they are framed as exchange/clearing-corporation measures. Page 179 separately lists grounds for broker suspension under the stockbroker regulations, which is a different action under different provisions. Note: Margin discipline in the F&O segment is enforced primarily by the exchange and the clearing corporation through penalties, position close-outs and use of the member's deposits/collateral.
